finding: Give-back of a lock just proven live is not retried on a Windows file-in-use error, so it falls through to deleting that live lock
why: The delta now routes a refreshed (live, possibly past-its-check) holder's lock into the bare os.rename(grave, lock) give-back; a transient PermissionError there drops to shutil.rmtree(grave), the stealer then mkdirs and loads while the holder runs os.replace, so 2 writers can lose an update, the sibling paths (_owner, utime, replace, unlink) all ride this error out through _patient.
fix: Wrap the give-back rename in _patient(os.rename, grave, lock), so only a real collision (FileExistsError) reaches the rmtree.
evidence: line 212 `if _owner(grave) != judged or not _is_stale(grave):  # replaced or refreshed since judged: give it back` then line 214 `os.rename(grave, lock)` (no _patient) and line 218 `shutil.rmtree(grave, ignore_errors=True)`; _patient docstring line 175: "retrying while Windows reports the path in use" (also reported by test-veracity: The owner-changed half of the give-back condition has no test; dropping it passes the whole suite) (also reported by test-veracity: No test covers the give-back rename failing for a refreshed grave, the branch that now deletes a live holder's lock)

finding: Comment says a steal judged before the refresh is given back, but a third writer that mkdirs the lock in the rename gap defeats the give-back
why: Between the stealer's rename and its give-back the lock path is empty: on POSIX os.rename(grave, lock) silently replaces the third writer's fresh empty lock folder (checked: rename onto an empty folder succeeds under WSL, raises FileExistsError on Windows), then that writer's write_text overwrites the restored owner, and on Windows the give-back fails and the live lock is deleted; either way a holder already past its check and the third writer publish concurrently, against the contract's "2 racing writers lose no update" guarantee widened to 3.
fix: Create the owner file exclusively in _acquire (open mode 'x', back off on FileExistsError) so a restored lock is never overwritten, and name the remaining Windows gap in this comment instead of claiming the steal is always given back.
evidence: line 280 `# Refreshed, then checked, after the slow write; a steal judged before the refresh is given back.`; _acquire line 244 `_patient((lock / "owner").write_text, token, "utf-8")`; scratch experiment: Windows `rename onto empty dir failed FileExistsError`, WSL `rename onto empty dir: replaced`

finding: The first item of `held` is a constant sentinel, so `held == [True, True]` partly asserts the fake's own recording
why: `held.append(True)` runs before the steal and records nothing observed, so the claim that the lock survived the publish-check steal rests only on the indirect `len(writes) == 1`, and the list mixes a flag with an observation under one name.
fix: Append `lock.exists()` after `manifest._steal_if_stale(lock)` in `contended`, and use a separate flag to make the steal run once.
evidence: test_team_manifest.py:393-395 `if writes and not held: held.append(True); manifest._steal_if_stale(lock)`; :407 `assert held == [True, True]`
